headline: High: shared filesystem writes and networked document processing create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no documented isolation or provenance controls, while Unstructured reads documents and can write outputs in a shared workflow. If Botpress ingests Unstructured-produced text or files as trusted instructions, prompt injection is plausible in default integrations. The pairwise pathway is inferred from docs-only profiles, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Botpress consumes Unstructured output from a shared file or message channel without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF the orchestrator passes raw document text from Unstructured into Botpress prompts, instructions can be hijacked.
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/template around Unstructured output.
Strip or escape instruction-like text before passing to Botpress.
Use a separate staging directory for parsed artifacts.
Review one sample end-to-end flow for prompt markers.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and allowlist-based prompt assembly.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Unstructured can read local documents and has allowlisted network egress, while Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented egress but also no documented data isolation. A shared workspace could expose documents to both agents, and Unstructured may transmit file contents to external APIs in some flows. That makes leakage plausible in default deployments, though not proven critical.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, documents can flow from Unstructured into Botpress outputs.
IF Unstructured sends parsed content to allowlisted external services, sensitive document text may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Place sensitive files in a separate workspace.
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs.
Limit Botpress access to redacted outputs only.
Check one document path for unintended uploads.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, and Unstructured also reads files and spawns subprocesses while supporting multiple instances. If they share a directory or mutable artifacts, concurrent writes and state corruption are likely without locking. Botpress lacks documented concurrency controls, so the overlap is dangerous by default in shared deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or partial writes can occur.
IF Botpress and Unstructured modify shared artifacts without locks, race conditions can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
Run one agent at a time on mutable resources.
Verify permissions on the shared path.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Unstructured produces parsed document text, and Botpress is a downstream conversational agent that may treat that text as authoritative. Without a verification step, parsing errors or hallucinated structure can cascade into incorrect support responses. The interaction is inferred from the profiles, so medium is warranted rather than low.
conditions: IF Botpress uses Unstructured output as source material without validation, errors can propagate.
IF parsed document fields are rendered directly into customer-facing replies, misinformation can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review for high-impact replies.
Compare parsed fields against the source document.
Add confidence thresholds before Botpress consumes extracted text.
Test one representative document for extraction errors.
requires-engineering: implement verification and citation checks in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with undocumented residency and retention controls, while Unstructured explicitly calls external docs/privacy endpoints and processes documents, images, and text. If regulated documents flow through both, mismatched retention or residency policies could create a compliance gap. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer documents are processed by both agents, retention and residency must align.
IF Botpress stores support transcripts longer than Unstructured's document-processing pipeline, policy mismatch exists.
mitigations: Review retention settings for both systems.
Restrict regulated data to one approved path.
Document data residency for each external endpoint.
Delete a test record end-to-end to confirm retention behavior.
requires-engineering: align contractual and technical compliance controls.
